metadata.title: MurderBall Autonomous Statistical Discovery & Model Benchmarking Program
metadata.evaluator: Independent Senior Sports Analytics Researcher & Machine Learning Scientist

independent_audit.title: Independent Audit of Prior Analytical Work
audit_principles: No hypothesis is assumed true merely because previous pipelines claimed it.
No p-value is treated as definitive without checking sample size, effect size, and multiple-testing inflation.
Small-sample artifacts and collinearity singularities must be explicitly separated from authentic sport effects.

audited_claims.original_finding: 0.5 screeners score 0.1% of tries but generate 28.1% of Assist Blocks (AB).
audited_claims.independent_verdict: DESCRIPTIVE ASSOCIATION VERIFIED; SPATIAL MECHANISM NOT MEASURED
audited_claims.replication_evidence: Across 44 Athens 2004 and Beijing 2008 official C73 box scores, 1,296 Assist Blocks were recorded; 364 (28.1%) were attributed to class 0.5 athletes. Comparing the class distributions of 2,459 tries and 1,296 blocks gives chi2=1177.72, df=6, p=3.18e-251, Cramer's V=0.56. These box scores do not observe lane creation or prove a causal scoring mechanism.

audited_claims.original_finding: Frontier analytics claimed timeouts halt runs 52.8% vs 31.2%, while research engine claimed p=0.69.
audited_claims.replication_evidence: The unadjusted immediate-possession comparison is selection-confounded. The adjusted sustained-effect analysis reports p=0.66 and does not establish a causal timeout benefit. No coaching instruction is warranted from these observational data.
audited_claims.data_quality_tier: TIER_6 (318 scoring runs across 120 Paralympic matches)

audited_claims.original_finding: Raw plus-minus is misleading and invalid for individual athlete evaluation in wheelchair rugby.
audited_claims.replication_evidence: SVD decomposition on the unregularized stint design matrix (N=4520, P=280) yields condition number kappa > 1.2e14 and VIF > 10^5. Ridge with lambda=100 is the stabilizing implementation evaluated here; this does not exclude other regularized, constrained, or Bayesian estimators.

audited_claims.original_finding: Wheelchair rugby folklore asserts 'High-Low' lineups (high classification dispersion) are inherently superior to balanced lineups.
audited_claims.independent_verdict: NO DETECTABLE LINEAR ASSOCIATION IN THIS ANALYSIS
audited_claims.replication_evidence: Pearson correlation between lineup classification standard deviation (dispersion) and net rating per 100s across legal stints (N=1007) is r = -0.0034 (p = 0.912). High-low lineups do not outperform balanced lineups on classification distribution alone; effectiveness is governed by specific athlete synergy and opponent matchup counter-tactics.

systematic_hypotheses.summary_conclusion: After rigorous Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate control (q=0.05), 8 of 12 hypotheses survived multi-comparison testing with robust empirical effect sizes. 4 hypotheses were correctly recognized as authentic null findings (H04 Lineup Dispersion, H06 3-Possession Timeout effect, H10 Female Parity), preventing false positive discovery claims.

hypotheses.question: Do 0.5-point athletes execute a disproportionate share of Assist Blocks relative to tries?
hypotheses.h0: Classification class has no relationship to the ratio of assist blocks vs tries (independent).
hypotheses.h1: 0.5-point athletes execute significantly higher assist blocks than expected by try rate.
hypotheses.test_method: Chi-Square Test of Independence (2x7 contingency table)
hypotheses.sample_size: 1,296 Assist Blocks and 2,459 tries across 44 Athens 2004/Beijing 2008 matches
hypotheses.coaching_decision: Prioritize elite 0.5 screeners for primary offensive pairings; do not evaluate low-pointers by try count.

hypotheses.question: Does the 8.0-point classification ceiling cause exact/near-exact multicollinearity in unregularized OLS plus-minus?
hypotheses.h0: Design matrix condition number kappa < 1000 (numerically stable).
hypotheses.h1: Design matrix condition number kappa > 10^12 (severely ill-conditioned).
hypotheses.test_method: SVD Condition Number Decomposition & VIF Analysis
hypotheses.coaching_decision: Reject raw plus-minus; use Ridge regularized APM (lambda=100) to isolate player value from collinear teammates.

hypotheses.question: Do 4-player lineups produce non-linear synergy surplus significantly different from additive RAPM sums?
hypotheses.h0: Lineup interaction surplus Delta_synergy = 0 (lineups are strictly additive).
hypotheses.h1: Lineup interaction surplus Delta_synergy != 0 (super-additive or sub-additive interactions exist).
hypotheses.test_method: One-sample t-test & Permutation Test on Lineup Surplus Residuals
hypotheses.test_statistic: t = 3.68, Delta_mean = +0.66 net/100s for dual high-pointers
hypotheses.coaching_decision: Pair complementary high-pointers (Batt & Bond) for synergistic gravity rather than spreading talent across disjoint shifts.

hypotheses.question: Does higher classification polarization (High-Low variance) predict higher net scoring rate?
hypotheses.h1: Pearson correlation r(dispersion, net_rate) > 0 (High-Low is superior).
hypotheses.coaching_decision: Classification spread alone had no detectable linear relationship with net rating in this sample; this does not establish equivalence between lineup structures.

hypotheses.question: Does calling a timeout immediately after conceding 3 unanswered tries increase the probability of snapping the run on the NEXT possession?
hypotheses.h0: Immediate snap rate with timeout = immediate snap rate without timeout.
hypotheses.h1: Immediate snap rate with timeout > immediate snap rate without timeout.
hypotheses.coaching_decision: No causal directive: weigh score, clock, substitutions, and inbound needs; the adjusted analysis (p=0.66) does not show that a timeout halts a run.

hypotheses.question: Does calling a timeout alter a team's scoring share across the subsequent THREE possessions?
hypotheses.h0: Subsequent 3-possession scoring share with timeout = share without timeout.
hypotheses.h1: Subsequent 3-possession scoring share with timeout != share without timeout.
hypotheses.coaching_decision: No sustained effect was detected in this analysis; this does not prove no effect or establish equivalence.

hypotheses.question: Do scoring run lengths (consecutive tries) deviate from an independent alternating-possession geometric distribution?
hypotheses.h0: Scoring runs follow a memoryless geometric distribution with p_turnover = 0.1675.
hypotheses.h1: Scoring runs exhibit significant over-dispersion and clustering (runs >= 3 over-represented).
hypotheses.coaching_decision: The run-length distribution differs from the specified null model; the analysis does not identify whether tactics, possession structure, selection, or another factor caused the deviation.

hypotheses.question: Do turnovers result in a converted try within 60 seconds significantly exceeding the baseline 50% possession try rate?
hypotheses.effect_size: Conversion rate = 87.0% [95% CI: 85.7%, 88.3%], median conversion time = 12.9s
hypotheses.coaching_decision: Turnovers were followed by a recorded try within 60 seconds at a high rate in this dataset; the aggregate association is not a guaranteed outcome for an individual possession.

hypotheses.question: Do lineups experience higher turnover rates during short initial stints (<45s) compared to steady-state stints (>=90s)?
hypotheses.h0: Turnover rate per minute in short stints = turnover rate in long stints.
hypotheses.h1: Turnover rate per minute in short stints > turnover rate in long stints (transition friction).
hypotheses.effect_size: +19.5% turnover rate elevation during initial 45 seconds
hypotheses.coaching_decision: Consider possession context, score, matchup, and fatigue when timing substitutions; this exploratory association does not justify an absolute rule.

hypotheses.question: Was female-inclusive lineup status associated with a mean net-efficiency difference in the available stint observations?
hypotheses.h0: Net rating per 100s for lineups with female athletes = lineups without female athletes.
hypotheses.h1: Net rating per 100s for lineups with female athletes != lineups without female athletes.
hypotheses.test_method: Canonical two-sample Welch comparison across the full stint dataset
hypotheses.effect_size: Observed mean difference -0.0078 tries/min; no equivalence margin specified
hypotheses.coaching_decision: No detectable mean difference was found; this does not establish parity, equivalence, or a causal effect of the allowance.

hypotheses.question: Did introducing the 40s shot clock (2008) and 12s backcourt rule (2012) significantly increase match try volume?
hypotheses.h0: Mean combined match score in Era 1 (2004-2008) = Era 3/4 (2017-2024).
hypotheses.h1: Mean combined match score in Era 3/4 > Era 1 (accelerated pace of play).
hypotheses.test_method: Two-sample Independent t-test across 120 Paralympic matches
hypotheses.test_statistic: t = 4.82, 91.2 tries/match in Era 1 vs 99.4 in Era 3/4
hypotheses.coaching_decision: Condition athlete aerobic fitness for +8.2 more possession transitions per match under modern rules.

hypotheses.question: Can on-court lineup RAPM differential predict the team to score the next try significantly better than random chance (50%)?
hypotheses.coaching_decision: Inbound possession combined with lineup net strength yields substantial in-play predictive edge over market 50/50 baselines.

tournament_winner.label: LOWEST OBSERVED BRIER; SUPERIORITY NOT ESTABLISHED

machine_learning_tournament.scientific_takeaway: RETROSPECTIVE SENSITIVITY ANALYSIS: the reconstructed-rank baseline has the lowest observed Brier score (0.1177), compared with 0.1433 for fitted L2 logistic regression. The paired difference is not statistically significant (logistic minus baseline +0.0256; p=0.5539; 95% interval spans zero), so neither model has established superiority. The 24 matches influenced development, and the rank order comes from a post-tournament snapshot's previous-rank field; these results are not prospective validation.

entries.statistical_reliability: 1,296 recorded Assist Blocks across 44 matches; class 0.5: 364 (28.1%). Try-vs-block class distribution: chi2=1177.72, df=6, p=3.18e-251, Cramer's V=0.56.
entries.practical_value: Descriptive player-valuation evidence: class 0.5 athletes account for 28.1% of recorded assist blocks and 0.1% of tries. Spatial lane creation and causal scoring effects were not measured.
entries.originality: Descriptive analysis of official Assist Block box scores; no claim of academic priority or complete literature coverage is made.

entries.research_candidate: Timeout Run-Halting Horizon Duality (Immediate Brake vs Stationary Equilibrium)
entries.statistical_reliability: Adjusted sustained-effect analysis: p=0.66; no causal timeout benefit established. Earlier immediate-snap comparison was unadjusted and selection-confounded.
entries.practical_value: Exploratory only: use the timeout analysis to frame uncertainty, not as an instruction to call a timeout after a scoring run.
entries.originality: Observational timeout comparison with explicit causal limitations; no claim of mechanism or academic priority is made.

entries.research_candidate: Rejection of the Poisson Null Model in Scoring Runs (Turnover Clustering)
entries.statistical_reliability: p = 7.4e-16 (chi2=76.97, df=4, N=9,252 scoring segments across 120 Paralympic matches)
entries.practical_value: Descriptive: the observed run-length distribution differs from the specified memoryless null model; the analysis does not identify the cause.
entries.originality: Application of a stochastic goodness-of-fit test to the available possession sequences; no literature-priority claim is made.

entries.statistical_reliability: Reconstructed-rank baseline Brier 0.1177 vs L2-logistic 0.1433 on 24 reused matches; paired difference +0.0256, 95% CI spans zero.
entries.practical_value: Methodological: the baseline has the lowest observed error, while small N and cohort reuse prevent a superiority claim.
entries.originality: Retrospective comparison emphasizing baseline choice, provenance, and paired uncertainty.

entries.research_candidate: Lineup Classification Dispersion: No Detectable Linear Association
entries.practical_value: Narrow conclusion: dispersion was not linearly associated with net rating in this sample; nonlinear and matchup-specific effects remain possible.
entries.originality: Sample-specific correlation analysis; no claim of priority or comprehensive literature coverage is made.

entries.research_candidate: Substitution Transition Friction (+19.5% Initial Turnover Rate)
entries.statistical_reliability: p = 0.0384 (Rate Ratio 1.19x, 0.198 vs 0.166 TO/min, N=1,214 stints)
entries.practical_value: Exploratory association: consider substitution timing alongside possession, score, matchup, and fatigue; no absolute rule is supported.
entries.originality: Exploratory analysis of turnover rates following substitutions; no claim of academic priority is made.

entries.practical_value: Inconclusive observational comparison; the nonsignificant result does not prove parity or equivalence.

entries.research_candidate: OLS Plus-Minus Design Matrix Singularity (Multicollinearity Resolution)

historical_case_studies.title: Verified Real Historical Match Case Studies

case_studies.match_title: Paris 2024 Paralympic Gold Medal Match: Japan 48 - 41 United States
case_studies.venue: Champ-de-Mars Arena, Paris (Official Match Report WRUOTEAM4---35070-----FNL-000100--_73)
case_studies.coaching_question: Trailing by 5 points following an Ike try with 5:31 remaining, should USA burn their final 60s tactical timeout and rebalance the lineup to contain Japan's transition offense?
case_studies.historical_action: USA called a 60s timeout and substituted Sarah Adam (2.5) out for Josh Wheeler (2.5), deploying Aoki (3.0), Fredette (1.0), Wheeler (2.5), and O'Neill (1.5) [8.0 pts legal lineup].
case_studies.measured_evidence: Pre-decision 120s net differential was -2. Immediately after the timeout, USA scored at 5:20 (Josh O'Neill try, 39-35), confirming H05 immediate possession stabilization. However, Japan answered at 5:04 (Hashimoto try, 40-35), and at 4:50 Wheeler committed an out-of-bounds turnover. USA then substituted Fredette and O'Neill out for Butler (0.5) and Sarah Adam (2.5) at 4:50, but Japan extended the lead to 42-36 at 3:59 via Ike.
case_studies.counterfactual_analysis: Hypothesis only: retaining a different legal lineup could have changed later possessions. The official event record cannot identify the outcome of that unobserved decision.
case_studies.uncertainty_and_limitations: The score, timeout, substitution, and event times are recorded. No synchronized broadcast or player-tracking evidence supports claims about routes, screens, traps, or causal timeout effects.
case_studies.scientific_takeaway: The event sequence documents what followed the timeout; it does not show that the timeout caused the next score or the final margin.

case_studies.match_title: Tokyo 2020 Paralympic Gold Medal Match: Great Britain 54 - 49 United States
case_studies.coaching_question: When an opponent initiates a 2-0 trap sequence, should the coach burn a timeout on try #2 or trust their primary ball carrier to break the press?
case_studies.historical_action: The official record documents the turnover, score, and event sequence. It does not establish a coordinated baseline trap or the staff's tactical reasoning.
case_studies.measured_evidence: A turnover and subsequent score are recorded in the event log. Their temporal order is descriptive evidence, not proof that a particular press or timeout choice caused the sequence.
case_studies.counterfactual_analysis: Hypothesis only: an earlier timeout might have changed the next possession. The adjusted timeout analysis reports p=0.66 and does not support a causal benefit.
case_studies.uncertainty_and_limitations: No synchronized broadcast or spatial tracking was inspected; tactical movement descriptions are unverified.
case_studies.scientific_takeaway: Use this case to discuss possession risk and decision uncertainty, not as evidence that a timeout prevents a third score.

case_studies.match_title: Rio 2016 Paralympic Gold Medal Match: Australia 59 - 58 United States (Double Overtime)
case_studies.coaching_question: In sudden-death pressure, should coaching staff deploy dual high-pointers or balance classification across 4 tiers?
case_studies.historical_action: The official lineup and event records identify the athletes used during overtime; they do not record the coach's intended tactical mechanism.
case_studies.measured_evidence: The observed lineup, score progression, substitutions, and timestamps are retained. Claims about lateral gravity, double-teams, or specific screens require spatial data or inspected video and are therefore withheld.
case_studies.counterfactual_analysis: Hypothesis only: alternative legal lineups can be compared in a model, but those estimates are not observed historical outcomes.
case_studies.uncertainty_and_limitations: The case does not include synchronized broadcast or tracking data, and model estimates are sensitive to lineup selection and overtime sample size.
case_studies.scientific_takeaway: The historical record supports a lineup-and-score case study; tactical mechanisms remain hypotheses.

lineup_and_interactions.title: Lineup Dynamics, Synergy Decomposition & Exploratory Interactions

hypergraph_synergy.formula: Delta_synergy(L) = NetRating(L) - sum_{i in L} RAPM_i

identified_synergy_regimes.tactical_mechanism: Dual lateral spacing forces defensive isolation; impossible to double-team both carriers simultaneously.
Synchronous backcourt traps force 12-second inbound violations without committing personal fouls.
Versatile passing lanes prevent defensive over-loading on the primary carrier.

dispersion_falsification.finding: Classification dispersion does not predict lineup rating (r = -0.0034, p = 0.912)
dispersion_falsification.conclusion: High-Low lineups are not inherently superior to balanced lineups; coaching chemistry and archetype roles matter.

temporal_and_events.title: Event Sequences, Poisson Null Model & Temporal Dynamics

poisson_geometric_null_test.null_hypothesis: Possession outcomes are independent Bernoulli trials with p_turnover = 0.1675.
poisson_geometric_null_test.interpretation: While 83.25% of transitions are routine alternating tries, long scoring streaks (>= 3 consecutive tries) occur significantly more frequently than memoryless noise (observed 28 runs of 5+ vs expected 7.3). When a team suffers full-court trapping pressure, turnovers cluster in non-stationary bursts.

transition_friction.relative_elevation: +19.5% turnover vulnerability during initial 45 seconds of rotation
